# Edmund Carrow

## Overview

- **Age:** Youth / schoolboy  <sub>[v5 c3 P12](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0012), [v5 c3 P14](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0014)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v5 c3 P12](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0012), [v5 c3 P13](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0013)</sub>
- **Origin:** Hollowmere  <sub>[v5 c3 P13](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0013)</sub>
- **Role:** Schoolboy at Glen St. Agnes school  <sub>[v5 c3 P14](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0014)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Walt  <sub>[v5 c3 P28](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0028)</sub>

## Appearance

Edmund is considered the most handsome among the children of Hollowmere, with well-shaped features and straight black hair. He features extraordinary, deep gray eyes that reflect a variety of emotions.

_Sources: [v5 c3 P12](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0012), [v5 c3 P13](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0013)_

## Personality

Edmund is an imaginative, dream-prone youth with an intense love of beauty. He is deeply devoted to poetry and nature, often preferring solitude and reading to active play or sports. Though initially considered timid or non-confrontational, he exhibits fierce moral conviction, loyalty, and unexpected resolve when defending others' honor.

_Sources: [v5 c3 P12](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0012), [v5 c3 P13](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0013), [v5 c3 P14](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0014), [v5 c17 P44](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0044), [v5 c17 P57](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0057), [v5 c17 P74](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0074)_

## Traits

- Imaginative  <sub>[v5 c3 P13](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0013)</sub>
- Lover of poetry  <sub>[v5 c3 P12](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0012), [v5 c3 P14](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0014)</sub>
- Loyal and protective  <sub>[v5 c17 P62](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0062), [v5 c17 P74](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0074)</sub>
- Fearful of facing troubles initially  <sub>[v5 c17 P71](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0071)</sub>

## Abilities

- Composing poetry  <sub>[v5 c3 P17](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0017)</sub>
- Distinctive literary style of speech ('talking book talk')  <sub>[v5 c3 P14](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0014)</sub>

## Goals

- To become a poet  <sub>[v5 c3 P14](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0014)</sub>

## History

Edmund grew up at Hollowmere alongside his siblings, spending much of his time reading poetry, enjoying nature in places like Fern Hollow, and quietly writing an epic poem modeled after Marmion. Due to his solitary nature and avoidance of fights, he was viewed as mild by his schoolmates at Glen St. Agnes. One evening, after Dan Coyle insulted his mother's writings and Grace Ashdown, Edmund confronted Coyle in a physical fight despite his internal fear and lack of experience. He emerged victorious, forcing Dan to take back his words. Following the fight, he met Mr. Ashdown, who praised his defense of honor, and returned home to be tended to by his mother.

_Sources: [v5 c3 P12](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0012), [v5 c3 P14](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0014), [v5 c3 P17](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0017), [v5 c17 P44](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0044), [v5 c17 P57](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0057), [v5 c17 P58](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0058), [v5 c17 P62](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0062), [v5 c17 P66](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0066), [v5 c17 P72](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0072), [v5 c17 P73](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0073)_

## Background by volume

- He took as his literary inspiration an 'Uncle Cedric' from the States who was formerly a student in Brierley.  <sub>[v5 c3 P14](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0014)</sub>
- He won a school award for poetry composition.  <sub>[v5 c4 P24](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0024)</sub>

## Quotes

> The angel of flowers has traveled across the earth today, summoning the blossoms. Those blue wings of his are visible to me on that hill near the forest.  <sub>[v5 c3 P20](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0020)</sub>

> Instead, my frequent dream is that I simply lift off the earth and hover above the hedges and the trees. The feeling is wonderful—and my thought is invariably, ‘Unlike every previous time, this is no dream. It's actually happening’—and then I awaken anyway, which is devastating.  <sub>[v5 c3 P24](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0024)</sub>

> Not constantly—and not frequently—yet on occasion—indeed, on occasion  <sub>[v5 c17 P65](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0065)</sub>

> I felt extremely scared, However, I do not intend to feel scared again, sir. Experiencing fear about troubles is more unpleasant than those troubles are.  <sub>[v5 c17 P71](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0071)</sub>

> Is every mother as kind as you are? Defending you is truly worth it.  <sub>[v5 c17 P74](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0074)</sub>
